dady-dady-1910-07-30.A1:
AN AWFUL CRIME AVENGED
Cruel Death of Little Bessie Morrison Followed by the Lynching of Her Murderers
Bonifay, July 31.—Two negroes, pleading vainly for their lives, were strung up by an infuriated mob between here and Dady yesterday afternoon, and while they were dangling from the ropes were perforated by the bullets of from fifty to seventy-five white men of the surrounding country.

The crime which caused the lynching is one of the most brutal ever known of in this country. The two negroes confessed to murdering little Bessie Morrison, the 12-year-old daughter of Mrs. Mary Morrison, who lives near Dady, in the extreme western end of Holmes county, whose body was found yesterday morning in a pool of water between the Morrison homestead and the little school at Dady.

The little girl started for school Friday morning alone, and the first intimation of a tragedy was when she failed to come home in the afternoon. After a reasonable time had elapsed a searching party was formed and after a quest lasting well into Friday night, found the mangled remains of the little girl in a pool of water in a swamp near the girl's home.

Her body was badly mangled and the shrubbery in the vicinity told of the one-sided fight of the girl against the two negro fields. After committing the murder the negroes dragged the body into a nearby swamp and threw her remains there, where they were found by the searching party.

As soon as the significance of the find dawned on the residents the searching party was transformed into a mob searching for the culprits. The sheriff at Bonifay was notified, and he, together with two assistants, went to Dady, where the two negroes were already arrested. A confession, giving some of the gresome details of the criminal assault and subsequent murder were made by the two men and the feeling was running high, but cool heads prevented a lynching on the spot.

The sheriff saw the only thing to be done was to rush the two men to the county jail, and at once started out for Dady, but the residents, who at this time were augmented by the arrival of others, got wind of the sheriff's plans and started in pursuit and overtook the sheriff in a lonely road, overpowering him and taking the two negroes to the nearest tree. Ropes were already provided for and it was only a short time before the negroes were swung up. Before their death the two reiterated their former confession.
dady-dady-1910-07-30.A5:
FOUR NEGROES LYNCHED
Whites Take Good Measure for Florida Murder.
De Funiak Springs, Fla., Aug. 1.—Following the lynching Saturday night of the negro charged with murdering little Bessle Morrison, at Dady, Fla., another negro, whose name is unknown, is reported to have been shot to death late to-day, charged with participation in the crime. Conflicting reports as to the number of negroes lynched have been received, but information indicates that to-day's victim made a total of four.

Mobile, Aug. 1.—The man hunt for "Bill" Walker, the negro, who early Sunday morning assaulted Mrs. J. O. Gibson, of Axis, Ala., and who later killed a negro, is to-night nearing the quarry. A posse headed by Sheriff Grago of Mobile apparently has the negro surrounded in a marsh, whither he was trailed by blood-hounds.
dady-dady-1910-07-30.A6:
FOUR NEGROES LYNCHED
FOR MURDER OF GIRL
FOR MURDER OF GIRL
Telephone Wires are Cut in Florida Section and Farmers are Pursuing Blacks.
(By Associated Press)

PENSA COLA, FLA., Aug. 1.—Telephone wires to the vicinity of Dade, Fla., were cut tonight and negroes were reported to be fleeing for their lives from that section. Business was reported suspended late today while farmers left their fields to join posses bent on carrying forward vengeance for the murder of the little school girl, Bessie H. Morrison, at Dade, Fir., who was slain last Friday.

Today is was reported that a negro had loaned an amulet for good luck to one of the colored men alleged to have slain the child.

This negro, whose name has not been learned here, was immediately captured and a rope put around his neck and as he swung from the limb of a tree, his body was shot almost to pieces.

According to information here, he is the fourth negro lynched for this murder. The cutting of the telephone wires made it impossible learn the cause of the hunt for negroes said to be in progress tonight.
dady-dady-1910-07-30.A8:
ONLY ONE NEGRO
LYNCHED AT DADY
Bonifay, Fla., Aug 2.—Latest reports from Dady, the scene of the lynching, is that only one negro was strung up by the mob. When the mob secured the two negroes from the officers they carried them to a nearby road where, after they had considered the case, they decided that one of the negroes should not be held for the murder of Bessie Morrison, and accordingly turned him over to the officers. As he is still suspected of having something to do with the murder, he is in jail.
dady-dady-1910-07-30.A10:
RIOTING AGAIN BREAKS FORTH Mob Repeats Work After School Girl's Murder. FOURTH NEGRO IS LYNCHED Victim Is Said to Have Given Aid to Tri. POSSES ARE SEARCHING SWAMPS FOR NEGRO WANTED FOR ASSAULT AND MURDER IN VILLAGE OF AXIS.
Pensacola, Fla., Aug. 1—(Special.)—Excitement is at fever heat in the northwestern portion of Holmes County tonight over the assault and murder of little Bessie Mae Morrison and the lynching of three negroes, Saturday night.

Another lynching occurred tonight, according to telegrams received here at 9 o'clock. The victim of the mob is said to have loaned a mule to one of the trio who committed the deed, knowing for what purpose it was wanted. He fled Saturday night but was caught in a swamp just at nightfall and hanged to a tree.

According to reports the community is in such a state of excitement that further shooting is expected at almost any minute. All business and work has been suspended and it is doubtful if any negroes are allowed to remain in the community.
dady-dady-1910-07-30.A12:
FOUR NEGROES DEAD.
Posses Are Scouring the Woods on Hunt for More.
Pensacola, Fla., Aug. 2.—Posses have been scouring the woods all night and early today in the vicinity of Dady, in the northwestern part of Holmes county, for negroes who may have knowledge of the assault on little Bessie Morison, which resulted in the death of the girl last Friday and the lynching of four negroes. Sheriff Kell, it is said, left Bonifay today with a posse and will endeavor to put an end to the trouble. It is stated also that several negroes have been fired on but no additional deaths are reported.
dady-dady-1910-07-30.A15:
QUIET AGAIN IN HOLMES COUNTY NO EVIDENCE AGAINST FOURTH NEGRO ARRESTED AND HE WAS NOT LYNCHED, BUT RELEASED BY POSSE. Special to the Journal.
DeFunjak Springs, August 2. Careful investigation leads to the belief that the rumor of the killing of the fourth negro accused of complicity in the assault and murder of Bessie Morrison, was untrue. No evidence was found to connect him with the crime and he was released. No further trouble is apprehended.

BABY BOUNCING MUST CEASE

THE PRACTICE IS INJURIOUS TO THE LITTLE ONES, ACCORDING TO EXPERTS, AND HAS CAUSED SEVERAL DEATHS.

By Associated Press.

New Orleans, Aug. 2.—The bouncing of babies on the knees of fond parents may be tabooed, in view of pathologic discoveries, according to Dr. S. W. Stafford, surgeon of the Charity Hospital at New Orleans. This statement was made in connection with reports that anterior poliomyelitis, a newly discovered infant malady, commonly known as infantile paralysis, is causing many deaths. Several such cases are now being treated in local hospitals. Dr. Stafford said that an injury to the spinal cord was most likely to result in the ailment and that the "bouncing" of babies could very easily produce such an injury.

dady-dady-1910-07-30.A17:
SIX NEGROES
Are Lynched in Florida Following Murder of Young White Girl.

Bonifay, Fla., August 2.—Two more Negroes were lynched today near Dady, Holmes county, making six who have paid the penalty for murder of Bessie Morrison, a fourteen-years-old white girl.

The little girl was seized by two Negroes last Friday afternoon, mistreated and then murdered. Two Negroes were lynched Saturday after they had confessed and said other Negroes knew of the crime.

The whites have cut the telephone wires from Dady, and it is difficult to get details, but reports agree that a reign of terror exists and that wholesale killing of Negroes is contemplated. Sheriff Bell and posse left here this afternoon for the scene to try to stop trouble, but it is not believed he will succeed, as the whites are said to be resolved to kill every Negro concerned in the crime against the little girl and to drive the others from the country.

THE BRUTAL MURDER OF A LITTLE GIRL IS QUICKLY AVENGED BY CITIZENS.
Little Victim.—Her Body Found in a Pool of Water.

Two negroes, pleading vainly for their lives, were strung up by an infuriated mob between Bonifay and Dady, Fla., Saturday afternoon, and while they were dangling from the ropes were perforated by the bullets of from fifty to seventy-five white men of the surrounding country.

According to the sheriff the mob was in such a mood that it could not be controlled, and he readily saw that white blood would be spilled if he did not turn the negroes over to them. Governor Mann of Virginia has appointed Former Gov. Claude A. Swanson of Chatham to succeed the late John W. Daniel in the United States Senate.

Representatives of locomotive engineers on fifty-six railroad systems west of Chicago met there Monday to consider plans which may result in a general demand for higher wages.

There are three applications in the hands of the city clerk. The committee to which was referred the budget of the board of education will probably report and the council will act.

Monday Quiet Day

Saturday night and Sunday were unusually quiet, and as a result there was little for the mayor to do in the police court this morning. The negroes in the city seem to be very wary of falling into the clutches of the law, and an epidemic of goodness has swept over Bessemer. There is a scarcity of negroes for the street gang, both on account of the few arrests and the cash payment of fines.

Veterans and Daughters Meet

Mrs. J. E. McAdory will lentertain both the United Daughters of the Confederacy and the United Confederate Veterans at her home tomorrow afternoon. All the veterans are urged to be present as an enjoyable time is assured. An address will be made by Joe C. Dubose. Arrangements have been made with J. H. Roden to carry the veterans to the home of Mrs. McAdory in an automobile and all who wish to go will meet at the Grand hotel at 3:30.

Interest in Discovery of Body

The citizens of Bessemer were much interested today when they learned that the body of a negro believed to have been Fred Spencer, the slayer of Capt. B. H. Young in April, had been found near Mulga. It will be remembered that Bessemer was stirred up at the time of the killing and posses of men from here searched the woods for Spencer. It is possible that he was lynched as the men declared that if he was found he would never reach the county jail alive.

Personal and General

The United Charities and hospital board of the Robinson hospital met at the home of Mrs. E. M. Owens this afternoon and transacted routine business. There was a full attendance and the meeting was very interesting. The reports of the hospital committees were heard and were very encouraging. The ladies feel hat they have realized success beyond their hopes in the management of the hospital.

Camp William Rose McAdory, U. C V., will meet at the city hall on next Saturday at 11 o'clock. The matter of entertaining the veterans at the county reunion will be discussed and plans made.

Mrs. A. R. Moore of Birmingham recently returned from the Orient, will deliver a lecture on "The Holy Land as it is Today." The lecture will take place at the high school auditorium on next Thursday evening.

Dr. J. A. B. Lovett, principal of the Lovett Training school, announces that the second annual session of the school will begin on October 3.

Nick Andrew and Miss Eugenia Metropolia were married at the home of the groom yesterday afternoon at 4 o'clock. The wedding attracted a large number of the Birmingham Greek colony and practically the whole of the Bessemer.

The Woman's Christian Temperance union will meet tomorrow afternoon at 4 o'clock at the First Baptist church.

The Forty-Two club will meet on Wednesday afternoon with Miss Dora Winters.

The Ladies Whist club will meet with Mrs. J. W. Carter Wednesday afternoon.

The baraca class of the First Christian church will serve ice cream and cake in the class room next Wednesday evening from 8 until 12 o'clock.
Miss Emma Lamar, who has been visiting Miss Lora Gunn for the past week, returned to her home in Montgomery today.
Mrs. C. K. Roberts of Chattanooga arrived today to spend the summer with her mother, Mrs. E. M. Owens.
